name: Muse Three.js 2: corpus tooling for a 1,000-scene run (Glimmer or Spark Open)
description: Builds the tooling to grow the dataset from the 51-brief pilot to 1,000 or more examples with either teacher: local Muse Glimmer or Muse Spark Open on Baseten: resumable brief growth, a chunked overnight driver, a repair pass for failed scenes, merge and de-duplication into the SFT files, and an optional screenshot quality score. Ralph writes the tools; the owner runs the long jobs.
standingRule: Offline-only PRD. The corpus run itself (about 18 hours without thinking at the measured 41 tok/s) is a manual gate. Ralph only builds and tests the tools with mocks and fixtures.
readFirst: docs/07-local-glimmer.md (measured speed, why concurrency stays 1, thinking vs no thinking)
scripts/*.py and scripts/lib/validate.mjs as left by PRD 1
manualGates: Owner runs `python scripts/run_corpus.py --target 1000 --chunk 50` overnight with `caffeinate -i` and reads data/pilot-report.md after each chunk
Owner picks a vision-capable local model and runs score_scenes.py on 20 scenes before trusting the scores

stories.title: gen_briefs: grow an existing brief set
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want to append new briefs to an existing set without reusing ids or leaking eval briefs so that the corpus can grow in stages.
steps: Add `--append` to scripts/gen_briefs.py: read data/briefs.jsonl (and the .eval file), continue ids after the highest existing one, skip anything near-duplicate of an existing brief (train or eval), and write only the new rows to the train file by appending.
In append mode never rewrite or re-split the eval file; create it only if it does not exist. `--count` means the final total of train briefs wanted.
Keep the balanced schedule from PRD 1 continuing from where the existing set stops (balance counts existing rows per domain).
Tests with a fake client: append adds only new ids, never touches existing lines or the eval file, rejects near-duplicates of eval briefs, and keeps domain counts within plus or minus 1.
criteria: Running append twice with the same fake client output adds zero rows the second time (asserted)
Existing briefs.jsonl lines are byte-identical after an append (asserted)
No brief in the train file is a near-duplicate of any eval brief (asserted)

stories.title: run_corpus.py: chunked, resumable overnight driver
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want one command that generates, validates and reports in chunks so that I can leave it running overnight and stop or resume it safely.
steps: Create scripts/run_corpus.py with `--target N --chunk 50 --teacher glimmer|spark [--think] [--model M] [--dry-run]`. Teacher presets: glimmer = --ollama-native, model muse-glimmer:30b-mlx, concurrency 1; spark = OpenAI route, model meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026, concurrency 4, --max-tokens 32000, and a required `--token-budget` per chunk (refuse to run spark without one).

Each loop: find the next chunk of briefs without a raw file, run teacher_generate.py with the teacher preset on that chunk via a temporary briefs file, then validate_scenes.mjs with --skip-done, then pilot_report.py; log to data/logs/corpus-<timestamp>.log and print an ETA from the measured seconds per scene.
Stop cleanly between chunks if the file data/STOP exists (and say so), and after Ctrl-C leave no half-written raw files.
`--dry-run` prints the chunks it would run and the exact commands without executing anything. Write tests for chunk selection, the STOP file and the dry-run output (patch subprocess so nothing runs).
criteria: `python scripts/run_corpus.py --target 100 --chunk 25 --dry-run` prints 2 chunks for a fixture of 50 done briefs and exits 0 without calling any process
A test shows chunk selection skips briefs that already have raw files and stops when data/STOP appears
docs/07-local-glimmer.md documents the overnight command, the STOP file and how to resume
`--teacher spark` without `--token-budget` exits non-zero before any call (asserted)

stories.title: repair_scenes.py: one repair attempt for failed scenes
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want failed scenes sent back to the model once with their error so that more of the corpus survives validation.
steps: Create scripts/repair_scenes.py: for each row in the validation report with reasons in {js_error, blank, static, bad_import, external_dep}, build a prompt containing the original brief, the previous HTML and the failure (console error text or reason), and ask the same model to return a corrected complete page in the same fenced format.

Reuse teacher_generate's call path (import it; do not copy) so both Ollama-native and OpenAI backends work; write results to data/raw_repair/<id>.json with a `repair_of` field and the original reason.
Never repair truncated or no_html rows, and never repair a scene twice (skip if data/raw_repair/<id>.json exists).

Tests with a fake call: only the allowed reasons are repaired, the prompt contains the error text, existing repair files are skipped, output shape matches teacher_generate raw files so the validator accepts the directory.
criteria: A fixture report with one row per reason yields repair calls only for the 5 allowed reasons (asserted)
`node scripts/validate_scenes.mjs --raw data/raw_repair ...` accepts the produced files (shape asserted in a test against the validator's field reads)
docs/03-pipeline-walkthrough.md describes the repair pass and says it runs once per scene

stories.title: build_dataset: merge repairs, de-duplicate, report stats
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want the SFT files to merge original and repaired scenes, drop near-duplicate code and report what was kept so that the dataset is clean and I know its size.
steps: Accept several teachers: `--raw` and `--report` may be given more than once (e.g. data/raw + data/validation.jsonl and data/raw_spark + data/validation_spark.jsonl). For a brief passing under several teachers keep one by `--prefer spark,glimmer` order; tag each row with `teacher` from the raw file's `model` field.
Extend scripts/build_dataset.py with `--repair-raw` and `--repair-report` (optional): prefer an original ok row, else a repaired ok row; tag each row with `source` (original or repair).

Drop near-duplicate scenes: shingle the JavaScript (5-token shingles) and drop a row whose Jaccard similarity to an already kept row is above 0.9 (keep the first by id); add `--min-chars` and `--max-chars` filters with defaults 800 and 60000.

Write data/sft/stats.json: counts by level, domain and source, dropped counts by reason (duplicate, too short, too long), and an estimated token count (characters divided by 3.5, labelled as an estimate).
Tests: repair preference, duplicate dropped, length filters, stats.json fields, output files unchanged for the no-repair case.
criteria: Two fixture scenes differing only in a colour constant are de-duplicated, two genuinely different ones both survive (asserted)
stats.json contains bySource, byLevel, byDomain, dropped and estimatedTokens with the estimate flagged as such
Running without the repair flags produces exactly the same train.jsonl as before this story for the PRD 1 fixtures
With two teachers passing the same brief only the preferred one is kept and stats.json has a byTeacher count (asserted)

stories.title: score_scenes.py: optional screenshot quality score
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want an optional blind quality score so that scenes that render but do not match the brief can be left out of training.
steps: Create scripts/score_scenes.py: for each ok row send the screenshot (base64) and the brief, never the code, to a local Ollama vision model chosen with a required `--model`, asking for a JSON object {score: 1-5, reason}; write data/scores.jsonl, resumable.
Before scoring, call Ollama /api/show for the model and refuse with a clear message if it does not list an image capability; do not assume any specific model has vision.
Add `--min-score` to build_dataset.py (default off) that drops rows below the threshold or without a score when it is set.
Tests with mocked HTTP: capability check refuses a text-only model, JSON parsing tolerates fenced and prose-wrapped output, resume skips scored ids, build_dataset honours --min-score.
criteria: Scoring a text-only model name fails fast with a message that names the missing capability (asserted)
The score prompt contains the brief and no HTML or JavaScript (asserted)
`--min-score 4` removes rows scored 3 and rows with no score in a fixture (asserted)
docs/06-budget-and-risks.md notes that the vision model is chosen by the owner and unverified
